There is a bug sending link commands for existing file paths. When we're
processing an inode
column2: we go over all references. All the new file paths are

column1: added to the ""new_refs"" list. And all the deleted file paths are added to
the ""deleted_refs"" list. In the end
column2: when we finish processing the inode

column1: we iterate over all the items in the ""new_refs"" list and send link commands
for those file paths. After that
column2: we go over all the items in the

column1: deleted_refs"" list and send unlink commands for them. If there are
duplicated file paths in both lists
column2: we will try to create them before we

column1: remove them. Then the receiver gets an -EEXIST error when trying the link
operations.
Example for having duplicated file paths in both list:
$ btrfs subvolume create vol
# create a file and 2000 hard links to the same inode
$ touch vol/foo
$ for i in {1..2000}; do link vol/foo vol/$i ; done
# take a snapshot for a parent snapshot
$ btrfs subvolume snapshot -r vol snap1
# remove 2000 hard links and re-create the last 1000 links
$ for i in {1..2000}; do rm vol/$i; done;
$ for i in {1001..2000}; do link vol/foo vol/$i; done
# take another one for a send snapshot
$ btrfs subvolume snapshot -r vol snap2
$ mkdir receive_dir
$ btrfs send snap2 -p snap1 | btrfs receive receive_dir/
At subvol snap2
link 1238 -> foo
ERROR: link 1238 -> foo failed: File exists
In this case
column2: we will have the same file paths added to both lists. In the

column1: parent snapshot
column2: reference paths {1..1237} are stored in inode references

column1: but reference paths {1238..2000} are stored in inode extended references.
In the send snapshot
column2: all reference paths {1001..2000} are stored in inode

column1: references. During the incremental send
column2: we process their inode references

column1: first. In record_changed_ref()
column2: we iterate all its inode references in the

column1: send/parent snapshot. For every inode reference
column2: we also use find_iref() to

column1: check whether the same file path also appears in the parent/send snapshot
or not. Inode references {1238..2000} which appear in the send snapshot but
not in the parent snapshot are added to the ""new_refs"" list. On the other
hand
column2: Inode references {1..1000} which appear in the parent snapshot but

column1: not in the send snapshot are added to the ""deleted_refs"" list. Next
column2: when

column1: we process their inode extended references
column2: reference paths {1238..2000}

column1: are added to the ""deleted_refs"" list because all of them only appear in the
parent snapshot. Now two lists contain items as below:
new_refs"" list: {1238..2000}
deleted_refs"" list: {1..1000}
Reference paths {1238..2000} appear in both lists. And as the processing
order mentioned about before
column2: the receiver gets an -EEXIST error when trying

column1: the link operations.
To fix the bug
column2: the idea is to process the ""deleted_refs"" list before

column1: the ""new_refs"" list. However
column2: it's not easy to reshuffle the processing

column1: order. For one reason
column2: if we do so
column3: we may unlink all the existing paths

column1: first
column2: there's no valid path anymore for links. And it's inefficient

column1: because we do a bunch of unlinks followed by links for the same paths.
Moreover
column2: it makes less sense to have duplications in both lists. A

column1: reference path cannot not only be regarded as new but also has been seen in
the past
column2: or we won't call it a new path. However

column1: idea to make find_iref() check a reference against all inode references
and all inode extended references because it may result in large disk
reads.
So we introduce two rbtrees to make the references easier for lookups.
And we also introduce record_new_ref_if_needed() and
record_deleted_ref_if_needed() for changed_ref() to check and remove
duplicated references early.
